structure.title: Business
structure.heading: ITEM 1. Business
structure.start_phrase: The statements in this report include forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.
structure.summary:
- Cautionary Statement: Forward-looking statements, key assumptions and uncertainties, and references to Risk Factors and MD&A.
- Company Overview: AMD as a global semiconductor company offering server CPUs/GPUs/DPUs, FPGAs/Adaptive SoCs, client CPUs/APUs/chipsets, discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoCs, and embedded products; occasional IP sales/licensing.
- Corporate and Investor Info: Incorporation, NASDAQ listing (AMD), headquarters and contacts, fiscal year convention, trademark disclosures, and website access to SEC filings and governance documents.
- Industry Context: Semiconductor and IC fundamentals and long-term trends in scaling and cost-per-function.
- Strategy: Focus on high-performance and adaptive computing across data center, embedded, client, and gaming via five pillars—compute leadership, expanding data center leadership, pervasive AI enablement, software and developer platforms, and custom silicon; integration of Xilinx and Pensando; chiplet and Infinity Architecture; four reportable segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded) plus All Other.
- Data Center Segment: Market need for performance, energy efficiency, and adaptability; products include EPYC server CPUs (9004 “Zen 4,” 7003 with 3D V-Cache, 7002), AMD Instinct data center GPUs (MI200, CDNA 2) with ROCm, Pensando DPUs and software, and FPGA/Adaptive SoC solutions (Versal, Zynq, Alveo accelerator cards, FaaS).
- Client Segment: Platform approach (CPUs, chipsets, GPUs/APUs); desktop CPUs (Ryzen 7000 “Zen 4,” Ryzen 5000 “Zen 3” with 3D V-Cache); notebook APUs (Ryzen 7000, 6000 “Zen 3+,” 5000 “Zen 3”); commercial CPUs (Ryzen PRO, Threadripper PRO, Athlon PRO); chipsets for AM5 (X670/B650 PCIe 5.0) and AM4 (X570/B550/A520/B450/A320), plus WRX80 for HEDT/workstations.
- Gaming Segment: Graphics architecture (RDNA 3, RDNA 2 features like ray tracing and Infinity Cache); semi-custom strategy and products (PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Valve Steam Deck APU); discrete GPUs (Radeon RX 7900 series RDNA 3 chiplet, RX 6000 RDNA 2), AMD Advantage notebooks, FSR 2.0; professional GPUs (Radeon PRO W6000).
- Embedded Segment: Target markets (industrial, automotive, medical, A&D, comms, networking, storage, thin clients); products include Embedded EPYC and Ryzen V-/R-Series; FPGA/Adaptive SoC families (UltraScale(+), 7 Series, Zynq/MPSoC/RFSoC, Versal portfolio); development kits and legacy families (Virtex, Spartan, CPLDs); design and software platforms (Vivado ML, Vitis, Vitis AI).
- Sales and Marketing: Direct and channel sales, distributors and reps, standard terms and warranties, branding across product lines, co-marketing and MDF programs.
- Customers and Channels: OEMs, cloud providers, ODMs, SIs, distributors, retailers, AIBs; engineering collaboration; one customer at 16% of 2022 revenue (Gaming); OEM focus segments; distributor protections; AIB/SI dynamics.
- Competitive Landscape: 
  - Data Center: Competes with Intel and NVIDIA; ARM-based server momentum.
  - Client: Competes primarily with Intel; ARM-based PCs emerging.
  - Gaming: NVIDIA leads discrete GPUs; Intel participates in iGPUs and discrete; AMD leads semi-custom consoles.
  - Embedded: Competes with Intel, Lattice, Microchip/Microsemi, Broadcom, Marvell, Analog Devices, TI, NXP, NVIDIA; competition from ASICs/ASSPs/CPLDs/DSPs.
- Research and Development: Focus on next-gen CPUs/GPUs, FPGAs/Adaptive SoCs, accelerators, SOMs/SmartNICs, software and tools; advanced process, packaging, heterogeneous integration; open-source contributions; US-led with global teams.
- Manufacturing and Supply Chain: Foundry partners (TSMC for HPC/FPGA/Adaptive SoC; GLOBALFOUNDRIES WSA for 12/14 nm; UMC and Samsung); outsourced board manufacturing; ATMP partners and JVs in APAC (including Tongfu, SPIL, KYEC).
- Intellectual Property: Robust patent portfolio and filings; cross-licensing and technology exchange; reliance on third-party software/IP for tools and products.
- Backlog and Seasonality: Predominantly PO-based with limited backlog except for semi-custom SoCs; historical 2H revenue seasonality.
- Human Capital: ~25,000 employees; mission/vision and high engagement; diversity, belonging, and inclusion initiatives and recognitions; leadership accolades; competitive total rewards and pay-for-performance; significant hiring in 2022; development and internal mobility.
- Environmental Matters: Compliance with global environmental and energy regulations; historical Superfund liabilities in Sunnyvale with settlements and ongoing remediation; accrued liability (~$3.9 million) and assessment of immaterial additional exposure.
- Risk Factors Summary (high level): 
  - Economic/Strategic: Intel’s market power, macro uncertainty, cyclicality, end-market demand shifts, customer concentration, COVID-19 impacts, competition, seasonality, IP protection, FX volatility.
  - Operational/Technology: Reliance on third-party manufacturing and materials, yield risk, product timing and transitions, dependency on semi-custom customers’ success, security vulnerabilities and cyber risks, ERP implementation risks, ordering/shipment uncertainties, third-party IP and platform component dependencies, reliance on Microsoft and broader software ecosystem support.

structure.title: Risk Factors
structure.heading: ITEM 1A. Risk Factors
structure.start_phrase: The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face.
structure.summary:
- Document scope: SEC Item 1A Risk Factors section with a summarized list and detailed discussion of risks, plus Item 1B (no unresolved staff comments).
- Economic and strategic risks:
  - Competitive pressure from Intel’s market dominance and aggressive practices; broader competition (including ARM-based solutions) and industry consolidation.
  - Semiconductor cyclicality; macroeconomic weakness, inflation, recession risk; PC market downturns and inventory corrections.
  - Demand volatility across Client, Gaming, Data Center; crypto-mining swings; reliance on a small number of significant customers.
  - COVID-19 impacts on workforce, demand, capital markets, and supply chains.
  - Seasonality and quarter-end sales concentration; IP protection challenges; foreign exchange exposure.
- Operational and technology risks:
  - Heavy reliance on third-party foundries and back-end services (TSMC for 7nm and below, GF for larger nodes, UMC, Samsung; ATMP JVs with Tongfu).
  - Wafer Supply Agreement with GF through 2025, with capacity allocations, purchase targets, pricing, prepayments, and potential penalties.
  - Supply constraints and dependencies on critical equipment, materials, substrates; limited/sole-source risks and cost/lead-time volatility.
  - Manufacturing yield risks and node transitions; potential delays or cost increases if yields fall short.
  - Product roadmap execution risks; dependence on customer design wins and launch timing; price erosion over product lifecycles.
  - Semi-custom SoC revenue tied to customer adoption and success (e.g., Sony PS5, Microsoft Xbox Series X|S).
  - Product security vulnerabilities; cybersecurity threats, data breaches, remote-work attack surface, regulatory scrutiny and compliance costs.
  - ERP system upgrade and operational continuity risks.
  - Demand forecasting, order/shipment uncertainties; excess/obsolete inventory risk and gaming/client charges noted in 2022.
  - Dependence on third-party IP, motherboards, software, memory, AIB partners; need for Microsoft OS/driver support.
  - Distributor/AIB concentration and incentives; price protection and return rights impacting revenue/margins.
  - Internal process/IT system resilience; compatibility issues; product defect and liability risks.
  - Supply chain efficiency; outsourced logistics and IT services performance risk.
  - Gray-market sales creating shadow inventory, margin pressure, and brand risk.
- Legal and regulatory risks:
  - Export controls, sanctions, tariffs, and trade restrictions (e.g., BIS Entity List, THATIC JV; licensing limits on advanced products like MI250/MI250X).
  - EAR/ITAR compliance requirements and potential license uncertainties or penalties.
  - Tax risks: realization of deferred tax assets, rule changes, audits, and potential liabilities affecting effective tax rate and cash flows.
  - Litigation exposure, including securities, consumer, and IP claims; potential injunctions, damages, redesign costs.
  - Environmental, conflict minerals, and forced-labor due diligence and compliance across global supply chains; evolving regulations and customer expectations.
- Merger, acquisition, and integration risks:
  - Integration of Xilinx and Pensando: operational, cultural, system, customer/vendor relationship, personnel retention, and synergy realization risks.
  - JV dependencies (e.g., ATMP JVs) and geopolitical/export constraints (THATIC).
  - Potential impairment of goodwill and other intangibles if performance or market conditions deteriorate.
- Liquidity and capital resources risks:
  - Debt and covenant restrictions under senior notes, Assumed Xilinx Notes guarantees, and $3B revolving credit facility; cross-default provisions.
  - Indebtedness effects on flexibility, competitiveness, and sensitivity to downturns; potential obligations under receivables sale/factoring arrangements.
  - Cash generation uncertainty for working capital, R&D, and strategic investments; possible need to reduce spend or raise capital.
- General risks:
  - Global operations exposure to geopolitical tensions (e.g., China–Taiwan, Ukraine conflict), sanctions, currency, logistics, exports, and local laws.
  - Natural disasters and climate-related events disrupting operations and suppliers.
  - Data privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA) obligations and penalties risk.
  - Potential impairments of technology licenses.
  - Talent attraction/retention challenges; stock-based compensation dynamics.
  - Stock price volatility and potential effects of stock repurchase programs.
  - Adverse impacts from worldwide political conditions on demand.
- Item 1B: No unresolved SEC staff comments.

structure.heading: ITEM 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments
structure.start_phrase: null.
structure.summary:
- Highlights risk factors around attracting and retaining qualified engineering, marketing, sales, and executive talent amid intense industry competition; reliance on stock-based compensation and its sensitivity to share price; and potential impacts from restructuring on retention.

structure.title: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.heading: ITEM 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase:
The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements as of December 31, 2022 and December 25, 2021 and for
each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2022 and related notes, which are included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K as well as with the
other sections of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, “Part II, Item 8: Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.”
structure.summary:
- Scope and purpose: Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) for AMD, covering 2022 vs. 2021 results, financial condition changes, off-balance sheet arrangements, and market risk disclosures, with references to prior-year MD&A for 2021 vs. 2020.
- Strategic developments: Completion of Xilinx acquisition (expanding into FPGAs, Adaptive SoCs/ACAPs, embedded markets) and Pensando acquisition (DPUs and software stack), reshaping AMD’s data center and embedded offerings.
- 2022 performance overview:
  - Net revenue rose 44% to $23.6B, driven by Data Center growth (EPYC), Gaming semi-custom sales, and Embedded (Xilinx), offset by a Client decline due to weak PC market and inventory corrections.
  - Gross margin fell to 45% (from 48%) due to Xilinx-related intangible amortization.
  - Operating income dropped to $1.3B (from $3.6B); net income fell to $1.3B (from $3.2B), largely from amortization and higher operating expenses.
  - Liquidity increased: cash/cash equivalents/short-term investments at $5.9B; total debt increased to $2.5B after new 2032 and 2052 senior notes; new $3.0B revolver and $3.0B commercial paper program established (undrawn).
  - Capital returns: $3.7B of stock repurchases; $6.5B remaining authorization.
- Product and technology roadmap execution:
  - Data Center: 4th Gen EPYC, 3rd Gen EPYC with 3D V-Cache, Versal ACAP VCK5000, Instinct MI210 and ROCm 5 ecosystem.
  - Embedded: Ryzen Embedded R2000, Kria KR260 Robotics Starter Kit.
  - Client: Ryzen 7000 Desktop (“Zen 4”) and AM5 platform; Ryzen 7000 Mobile; Ryzen 6000 Mobile (“Zen 3+”, RDNA 2 graphics); Ryzen 5000 C-Series; Threadripper PRO 5000 WX; Ryzen PRO 7030 Mobile.
  - Gaming: Radeon RX 7900 XTX/XT (RDNA 3), RX 6000 series refresh, Radeon PRO W6400.
- COVID-19 impact: Limited disruptions in 2022; ongoing monitoring.
- Critical accounting estimates: Detailed methodologies and judgments for revenue allowances (variable consideration), inventory valuation (LCNRV, excess/obsolescence), business combinations (fair value allocation), goodwill impairment testing (income/market approaches), long-lived/intangible asset impairment, and income taxes (valuation allowances, uncertain tax positions).
- Segment results (new 2022 structure: Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded):
  - Data Center: Revenue up 64% to $6.0B; operating income up to $1.85B on higher EPYC sales.
  - Client: Revenue down 10% to $6.2B (lower units, higher ASPs); operating income down to $1.19B.
  - Gaming: Revenue up 21% to $6.8B (semi-custom strength; weaker graphics); operating income up slightly to $953M.
  - Embedded: Revenue up sharply to $4.6B; operating income up to $2.25B, driven by Xilinx.
  - All Other: $5.0B operating loss mainly from $3.5B acquisition-related intangible amortization, $1.1B stock-based comp, $452M acquisition-related costs.
- Consolidated expense/margin drivers:
  - R&D up 76% to $5.0B; SG&A up 61% to $2.3B; $3.6B total amortization of acquisition-related intangibles (COGS and Opex).
  - Licensing gain of $102M from THATIC JV milestones/royalties.
  - Interest expense increased to $88M from new and assumed notes.
  - Other income decreased due to equity investment valuation changes; offset by higher interest income.
  - Income tax benefit of $122M (effective rate -10%) driven by lower pre-tax income, FDII benefit, and R&D credits; continued ~$2.1B valuation allowance.
  - International sales were 66% of revenue; sales largely USD-denominated.
- Liquidity and cash flows:
  - Operating cash flow: $3.6B; key working capital movements included higher inventories, receivables, and supply prepayments, partly offset by higher payables and accruals.
  - Investing cash flow: $2.0B provided (Xilinx cash acquired, maturities of investments; offset by Pensando acquisition, new investments, capex).
  - Financing cash flow: $(3.3)B (share repurchases, tax withhold repurchases, debt repayment; partially offset by new debt issuance and employee plan proceeds).
  - Commitments: $8.6B unconditional purchase commitments ($6.5B due in 2023); belief in sufficient liquidity via cash, operations, revolver, and CP program.
  - No off-balance sheet arrangements.
- Market risk disclosures (Item 7A):
  - Interest rate risk: Short-duration investment portfolio; hypothetical 50 bps move changes fair value by ~$2.9M; long-term debt is fixed-rate.
  - Default risk: Conservative, highly rated, liquid securities; active monitoring.
  - Foreign exchange risk: Costs and balances in multiple currencies; USD sales predominance; hedging program with FX forwards (notional exposure by currency disclosed; all maturities within 18 months).

structure.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosure About Market Risk
structure.heading: ITEM 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosure About Market Risk
structure.start_phrase: Our exposure to market risk for changes in interest rates relates primarily to our investment portfolio and long-term debt.
structure.summary:
- Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
  - Interest rate risk: Cash and investments are held in short-maturity, high-quality instruments; interest income varies with short-term rates. A hypothetical 50 bps change at December 31, 2022 would move the fair value of cash equivalents and investments by about $2.9 million. All long-term debt is fixed-rate, so reported interest expense exposure is minimal. Ongoing monitoring planned.
  - Default risk: Mitigated by investing only in high-credit-quality, largely A-rated, short-maturity debt with active secondary markets and issuer exposure limits. Conservative approach focused on capital preservation, though risks cannot be fully eliminated.
  - Foreign exchange risk: Costs/assets/liabilities in multiple currencies while sales are primarily in USD. Uses non-speculative FX forwards maturing within 18 months to hedge exposures. As of December 31, 2022, total notional $2.421 billion with an estimated net fair value loss of $28 million (vs. $1.185 billion notional and $2 million loss at December 25, 2021). Currency breakdown includes notable positions in Chinese Renminbi, Canadian Dollar, Indian Rupee, Taiwan Dollar (losses), and gains in Singapore Dollar and Euro.

- Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
  - Consolidated Statements of Operations for 2022, 2021, 2020: Net revenue grew to $23.6 billion (from $16.4 billion in 2021 and $9.8 billion in 2020); gross profit $10.6 billion in 2022. Significant 2022 amortization of acquisition-related intangibles ($1.448 billion in cost of sales and $2.100 billion in operating expenses). Operating expenses increased (R&D $5.0 billion; marketing, general and administrative $2.3 billion). Operating income was $1.26 billion (down from $3.65 billion in 2021). Net income was $1.32 billion; basic/diluted EPS were $0.85/$0.84. Income tax showed a net benefit in 2022; shares outstanding increased year over year.

structure.title: Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
structure.heading: ITEM 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
structure.start_phrase: See accompanying notes to consolidated financial statements.
structure.summary:
- Scope: Item 8 of AMD’s Form 10-K, presenting audited consolidated financial statements for fiscal years 2022, 2021, and 2020, with notes, segment data, auditor reports, and controls and procedures.

- Results of operations:
  - 2022 net revenue $23.6B (up from $16.4B in 2021), gross profit $10.6B.
  - Operating income $1.3B (down from $3.6B) due mainly to $3.5B amortization of acquisition-related intangibles and higher R&D and SG&A.
  - Net income $1.3B; diluted EPS $0.84 (vs. $2.57 in 2021).
  - Comprehensive income reflects hedge-related OCI losses.

- Financial position (Dec 31, 2022 vs. Dec 25, 2021):
  - Total assets $67.6B (from $12.4B), driven by Xilinx acquisition: goodwill $24.2B and intangibles $24.1B.
  - Cash and equivalents $4.8B; short-term investments $1.0B; inventories $3.8B.
  - Stockholders’ equity $54.8B (from $7.5B).
  - Total debt $2.5B (assumed Xilinx notes and new 2032/2052 notes); deferred tax liabilities $1.9B.

- Cash flows (2022):
  - Operating cash flow $3.6B.
  - Investing cash flow +$2.0B (cash from Xilinx acquisition net of Pensando, securities activity, capex).
  - Financing cash flow -$3.3B (share repurchases $3.7B, new debt $1.0B, repayment of $312M notes).

- Significant accounting policies and changes:
  - Revenue recognition: point-in-time for non-custom; over time (cost-based input) for semi-custom; licensing recognized over time or point-in-time depending on terms.
  - Inventory valued at lower of cost or NRV with reserves for excess/obsolescence.
  - 2022 change to recognize deferred taxes for GILTI, increasing deferred tax liabilities and lowering tax expense; reclassification of tax interest to income tax line.

- Segment reporting (revised in 2022): Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded; All Other captures amortization of acquisition intangibles, SBC, acquisition costs, and licensing gains.
  - 2022 revenue by segment: Data Center $6.0B; Client $6.2B; Gaming $6.8B; Embedded $4.6B.
  - Operating income (loss): Data Center $1.85B; Client $1.19B; Gaming $0.95B; Embedded $2.25B; All Other $(4.98)B.
  - Geographic revenue led by U.S., China (incl. HK), Japan; one customer at 16% of revenue.

- Business combinations:
  - Xilinx (closed Feb 14, 2022): purchase consideration $48.8B; identifiable intangibles $27.3B (developed technology and customer relationships predominant), goodwill $22.8B allocated mainly to Embedded and Data Center; Xilinx contributed $4.6B revenue and $2.25B operating income (before All Other charges). Assumed unvested RSUs (~$1.2B fair value).
  - Pensando (closed May 26, 2022): consideration $1.66B; intangibles $349M (including $220M IPR&D); goodwill $1.10B to Data Center.

- Intangibles and goodwill:
  - 2022 amortization expense $3.5B; remaining amortization expected at $2.8B (2023), $2.3B (2024), declining thereafter.
  - Goodwill $24.2B: Embedded $21.1B, Data Center $2.9B, Gaming $0.2B; no impairment.

- Related parties:
  - ATMP JV (15% owned): 2022 purchases $1.7B; payables $463M; equity income $14M.
  - THATIC JV: licensing gains $102M; compliance with U.S. Entity List.

- Capital structure and liquidity:
  - Debt: assumed Xilinx 2024 ($750M) and 2030 ($750M) notes; new AMD senior notes $500M (2032) and $500M (2052); repaid $312M 7.50% notes at maturity.
  - $3B five-year revolving credit facility (undrawn) and $3B commercial paper program (no outstanding balance at year-end).
  - Future debt maturities concentrated in 2024 and long-dated thereafter.

- Investments and fair value:
  - Cash equivalents and AFS debt securities in money market funds, commercial paper, U.S. Treasuries, agencies; Level 1 and 2 fair value hierarchy.
  - FX cash flow hedges outstanding notional $1.9B; fair value liability $27M.
  - Non-marketable equity securities $137M.

- Credit risk:
  - Diversified customer base; one customer at 18% of receivables; high-grade investment policies; large bank hedge counterparties.

- Earnings per share:
  - 2022 basic shares 1,561M; diluted 1,571M; anti-dilutive shares excluded.

- Equity and stock-based compensation:
  - Issued 429M shares for Xilinx; repurchased 36.3M shares for $3.7B; $6.5B authorization remaining.
  - 2022 SBC expense $1.08B pre-tax; details on options, RSUs/PRSUs, ESPP, and unrecognized compensation cost.

- Retirement benefits: U.S. 401(k) with 75% match up to 6%; 2022 contributions $47M.

- Income taxes:
  - 2022 tax benefit $(122)M; effective rate (10%); driven by FDII, R&D credits, GILTI deferred tax effects, and R&D capitalization.
  - Deferred tax assets $4.5B (including capitalized R&D); liabilities $4.3B (mainly acquired intangibles and GILTI); net position a liability.
  - Valuation allowance $2.08B; unrecognized tax benefits $1.36B; audits ongoing (U.S. federal years from 2008 open; pre-acquisition Xilinx under IRS audit).
  - Singapore DEI incentive through 2031 (5% rate) noted.

- Other income (expense), net: higher interest income; equity investment losses; prior-year debt redemption impacts.

- Commitments and guarantees:
  - Operating lease ROU assets/liabilities with weighted average term ~6 years; 2022 lease expense $118M.
  - Unconditional purchase commitments $8.6B (primarily wafers/substrates and licenses).
  - Warranty reserve $65M; standard indemnities disclosed.

- Contingencies:
  - IP litigation matters with Quarterhill/Polaris, Monterey, Analog Devices (resolved in 2022), and Future Link; licenses or defenses in place; no material adverse expected.
  - Environmental remediation at three Sunnyvale Superfund sites; $3.9M liability recorded.

- Auditor reports:
  - Ernst & Young LLP issued unqualified opinions on the financial statements and on internal control over financial reporting.
  - Critical audit matters: inventory valuation judgments and fair value measurement of Xilinx acquisition intangibles.

- Controls and procedures:
  - Management concluded disclosure controls and procedures were effective; internal control framework and inherent limitations described.

structure.summary:

- The company is integrating Xilinx and Pensando operations, processes, and systems into its control environment and is monitoring controls during this integration.
- Item 9B: Other Information—The Russian FSB is a blocked party under Executive Order 13382; OFAC General License No. 1B permits certain limited transactions related to IT product imports into Russia.
- Xilinx (acquired Feb 14, 2022) had previously authorized Russian resellers to file notifications/apply for FSB import licenses under the OFAC General License; additional filings occurred post-acquisition in the quarter ended March 26, 2022.

- Exhibit listings include: the Principal Financial Officer’s Section 906 Sarbanes-Oxley certification and a full set of Inline XBRL materials (instance, schema, calculation, definition, label, presentation) plus the cover page interactive data embedded within Inline XBRL.
- Notes on exhibits indicate: certain management/compensatory agreements; portions omitted under confidential treatment or because not material and competitively sensitive; AMD will provide copies of exhibits upon request and reimbursement of reasonable expenses.
- Item 16 (Form 10-K Summary): Not applicable.
- Signatures section: The report is executed pursuant to Sections 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, dated February 27, 2023. Signatories include Lisa T. Su (Chair, President, and CEO; also Attorney-in-Fact), Jean Hu (EVP, CFO and Treasurer; Principal Financial Officer), Darla Smith (Corporate VP, Chief Accounting Officer; Principal Accounting Officer), and directors including Lead Independent Director Nora M. Denzel, Mark Durcan, Mike P. Gregoire, Joe A. Householder, John W. Marren, Jon A. Olson, Abhi Y. Talwalkar, and Beth W. Vanderslice.

structure.start_phrase:
Pursuant to the requirements of Section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the registrant has duly caused this report to be signed
on its behalf by the undersigned, thereunto duly authorized.
structure.summary:
- Signatures: The Form 10-K is signed on February 27, 2023 by Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD), with Lisa T. Su (Chair, President and CEO) signing on behalf of the registrant. Additional signatures include Principal Financial Officer Jean Hu, Principal Accounting Officer Darla Smith, and multiple directors. Lisa T. Su also signs as attorney-in-fact for certain directors.
- Exhibit 18.1: Ernst & Young LLP letter noting AMD’s change in accounting classification for tax interest expense—from Interest expense to the Income tax provision (benefit) line—in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. While no authoritative “preferable” classification exists, EY concludes the change is an acceptable alternative and preferable based on AMD’s business judgment.
- Exhibit 21: Comprehensive list of AMD subsidiaries as of December 31, 2022, covering domestic (e.g., Xilinx, Inc., Pensando Systems, Inc., Solarflare Communications, Inc., SeaMicro, Inc.) and foreign entities across numerous jurisdictions (e.g., China, India, Ireland, Japan, Malaysia, Singapore, U.K.). Includes detailed ownership structures, percentages, and notes on inactive or dissolving entities.
- Exhibit 23: Consent of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm (Ernst & Young LLP) permitting incorporation by reference of their reports into various AMD registration statements (multiple Forms S-8, S-4 related to the Xilinx merger, and Form S-3).
- Exhibit 24: Power of Attorney authorizing Lisa T. Su, Jean Hu, and Harry A. Wolin to sign and file the 2022 Form 10-K and any amendments, with signatures and dates from AMD’s officers and directors.
- Exhibit 31.1 and 31.2: Sarbanes-Oxley Section 302 certifications by the CEO and CFO attesting to their review of the 10-K, fair presentation of financials, and the effectiveness of disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting, including disclosure of changes, deficiencies, and fraud.
- Exhibit 32.1 and 32.2: Sarbanes-Oxley Section 906 certifications by the CEO and CFO that the 10-K complies with Exchange Act requirements and fairly presents the company’s financial condition and results of operations.
- Dates and address: Most documents dated February 27, 2023; some director signatures dated February 3–10, 2023. AMD’s address appears as 2485 Augustine Drive, Santa Clara, California 95054.
